what_its_for: Ketotifen is used to relieve itchy, red, and watery eyes caused by allergies. It works by blocking histamine, the chemical in your body that causes allergy symptoms. It is available as eye drops for eye allergies and as a tablet or syrup for preventing asthma symptoms related to allergies.
how_to_take: FOR EYE DROPS: Wash your hands before using the drops. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to make a small pocket, and place the prescribed number of drops inside. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes. Do not touch the dropper tip to your eye, fingers, or any surface to keep it clean. If you wear soft contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 10 minutes before putting them back in. FOR TABLETS OR SYRUP: Take by mouth with or without food. Swallow tablets whole with a glass of water.
dosing: EYE DROPS (adults and children 3 years and older): Typically 1 drop in the affected eye(s) twice a day, about 8 to 12 hours apart. TABLETS (adults and children over 3 years): Usually 1 mg (1 tablet) twice daily, taken with food. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose and slowly increase it. Always follow the exact dose your doctor or pharmacist has prescribed for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take or use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or use extra doses to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep away from direct sunlight, heat, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not use eye drops if the liquid looks cloudy or has changed color. Discard eye drops within 4 weeks of opening even if there is still solution left in the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Do not wear soft contact lenses while your eyes are red or irritated from allergies. Avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface to prevent contamination. Ketotifen tablets may cause drowsiness, especially when you first start taking them, so avoid driving a car, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking ketotifen tablets, as it can increase drowsiness.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: severe eye pain or increased redness after using the drops, vision changes or blurred vision that does not go away, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, severe dizziness or confusion, eye discharge or signs of eye infection, or if your symptoms do not improve after a few days of use.
when_it_works: Eye drops usually start to relieve itching within a few minutes of use. For tablets or syrup used to prevent asthma or allergy symptoms, it may take several weeks (up to 10 to 12 weeks) before you notice the full benefit. Do not stop taking the tablets suddenly without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better.
special_populations: CHILDREN: Eye drops are approved for children 3 years and older. Tablets should be given to children only under a doctor's supervision. PREGNANT OR BREASTFEEDING WOMEN: Talk to your doctor before using ketotifen if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety for these situations is not fully established. ELDERLY: Older adults may be more sensitive to the drowsy effects of ketotifen tablets and should use caution. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
